title: Cosmo/Wanda Top 20 vs Top 50: Live Performance Verdict

title: Cosmo/Wanda Top 50 Stalled at 11 Closed Trades; 20-Pair Dynamic Universe Retains Structural Edge and Power-Ranking Dominance
content:

content:

title: Static Top-20 Freeze Would Not Materially Converge to Top-20 Metrics: Dynamic Rebalancing Is the Structural Edge
content:
Focus question: If Cosmo/Wanda Top 50 were reconfigured to a static whitelist limited to the current top 20 highest-market-cap pairs (matching the dynamic universe's composition but frozen), would its per-trade ROI and unrealized-to-realized ratio converge materially toward Top 20 levels, or is the dynamic rebalancing mechanism itself necessary to realize the structural edge?

Local indexed research and live-site evidence indicate that a frozen static top-20 whitelist would improve on Top 50's current static-50 pathology but would NOT materially converge to Cosmo/Wanda Top 20's per-trade ROI (~1.75%) or its balanced sub-1.0× unrealized-to-realized ratio. As of the latest indexed snapshot, Top 50 (Bitget/USDT, static 50-pair whitelist) shows an average ROI of roughly ~1.24–1.26% and an unrealized-to-realized ratio materially above 1.0× (approximately 1.8–2.9×), while Top 20 (Hyperliquid/USDC, dynamic MarketCapPairList with number_assets: 20 and refresh_period: 86400) maintains a stable ~1.75% average ROI and an unrealized-to-realized ratio of ~0.78×. Prior research updates identify Top 50's static 50-pair whitelist as the root source of structural drag because it 'captures quick scalps in lower-tier pairs that accumulate deep adverse carry.' Freezing the whitelist to the current top 20 would remove that lower-tier carry source and likely produce a modest uplift in per-trade ROI and a lower unrealized-to-realized ratio relative to the 50-pair baseline. However, those same updates explicitly credit Top 20's dynamic MarketCapPairList with 'far more actionable exit opportunities and better liquidity alignment,' and earlier research concluded that merely matching exchange/currency and exceeding 20 closed trades is insufficient to close the gap because static-whitelist drag persists. By further inversion, freezing even the correct top-20 composition abandons the daily liquidity-maintenance mechanism; as market-cap rankings shift, the static list would decay, retaining pairs that fall out of the top tier while omitting newly rising liquid ones. Residual dispersion from Bitget/USDT execution conditions would remain a secondary, non-dominant confounder, but the absence of daily rebalancing is expected to prevent convergence to Top 20's balanced carry profile and stable ROI floor.

title: Static Top-20 Freeze Insufficient: Dynamic Rebalancing Is the Structural Edge
content:
Focus question: If Cosmo/Wanda Top 50 were reconfigured to a static whitelist limited to the current top 20 highest-market-cap pairs (matching the dynamic universe's composition but frozen), would its per-trade ROI and unrealized-to-realized ratio converge materially toward Top 20 levels, or is the dynamic rebalancing mechanism itself necessary to realize the structural edge?

Local indexed research and live-site evidence indicate that a frozen static top-20 whitelist would improve on Top 50's current static-50 pathology but would NOT materially converge to Cosmo/Wanda Top 20's per-trade ROI or its balanced sub-1.0x unrealized-to-realized ratio. Current live-site standings show Top 50 (Bitget/USDT, static 50-pair whitelist) at ~1.24% average ROI with an unrealized-to-realized ratio of roughly 3.3x realized gains (-29.24 USDT unrealized vs +8.83 USDT realized), while Top 20 (Hyperliquid/USDC, dynamic MarketCapPairList with number_assets: 20 and refresh_period: 86400) maintains ~1.75% average ROI and a ratio of ~0.86x. Prior research updates identify Top 50's static 50-pair whitelist as the root structural drag because it 'captures quick scalps in lower-tier pairs that accumulate deep adverse carry.' Freezing the whitelist to the current top 20 would remove that lower-tier carry source and likely produce a modest uplift relative to the 50-pair baseline. However, those same updates explicitly credit Top 20's dynamic MarketCapPairList with 'far more actionable exit opportunities and better liquidity alignment,' and earlier counterfactual research concluded that static-whitelist drag persists even when exchange/currency settings are matched. By inversion, freezing the composition abandons the daily liquidity-maintenance mechanism; as market-cap rankings shift, the static list would decay, retaining pairs that fall out of the top tier while omitting newly rising liquid ones. Therefore, while a static top-20 whitelist would reduce adverse carry compared with the 50-pair version, the dynamic rebalancing mechanism itself is necessary to realize the full structural edge. Residual dispersion from Bitget/USDT execution conditions would remain a secondary, non-dominant confounder.

title: RemotePairlists/Custom pairlists are coming
content: Your research into the static top 20 hypothetical is deeply appreciated as it reminded me that I do not accept the static pairlist conditions we were forced into by rate limits to CoinGecko when spinning up multiple instances using dynamicpairlists. Now we have custom pairlists, a new high level artifact of this environment which will soon be highly relevant to all strategies. Defining optimal universes suited to strategies in unique ways beyond "most volume" or "most marketcap" is at least one big focus of study going forward. We have implemented this already, the effects still need time to percolate. The top level teams of the competition won't be updated to custom pairlists until season 2, but I believe development league teams will be getting custom pairlists as soon as possible.

title: Phased Non-Market-Cap Pairlist Criteria for Cosmo/Wanda: Dispersion, Liquidity Depth, and Volatility Slope
content:
Focus question: Given that dynamic rebalancing is confirmed as the dominant causal edge and custom pairlists are now available, which non-market-cap selection criteria (e.g., realized volatility slope, liquidity depth, or correlation dispersion) should be tested as the next iteration of dynamic universe construction to see if they can improve upon the current MarketCapPairList edge for Cosmo/Wanda-style strategies?

Local indexed research confirms that Cosmo/Wanda Top 20's structural edge (~1.75% per-trade realized ROI, ~0.86–0.93× unrealized-to-realized ratio) is driven by the daily liquidity-maintenance mechanism of dynamic rebalancing, not the 20-pair count or Hyperliquid venue. With custom RemotePairlists now implemented, the incumbent MarketCapPairList (refresh_period: 86400, number_assets: 20) can be actively superseded. Three non-market-cap criteria, validated by local strategy artifacts and development-league telemetry, should be tested in a phased A/B sequence.

1) Cross-Sectional Dispersion / Divergence_z (Jade-validated, Maverick-cautioned)
Development-league telemetry shows Jade (C shift, +1.86 realized, 86% win rate) successfully employs basket dispersion (standard deviation of basket returns) and divergence_z to trade BTC-vs-basket outliers. Conversely, Maverick (D shift, –1.78 realized, 129 trades/24h) proves that raw cross-sectional z-scoring without liquidity or volatility gating degrades into churn. Recommendation: use Jade-style dispersion and divergence_z as a ranking input, not a standalone trigger, and require a minimum volatility context to avoid Maverick's noise pathology.

2) Liquidity Depth / Exit Actionability (Top-20 carry attribution)
Prior updates attribute Top 20's superior carry to "far more actionable exit opportunities and better liquidity alignment." Rather than inferring liquidity from market-cap rank, an explicit dynamic filter should incorporate a liquidity-depth proxy (e.g., bid-ask spread tightness relative to ATR, or estimated slippage on entry) as a hard floor. Power-ranking notes on C&W-20 highlight ~$63.49 in unrealized drag subsidizing open swing positions; liquidity filtering may exclude names that trap capital in adverse excursions where the strategy cannot realize profits efficiently.

3) Realized Volatility Slope / Regime State (Downforce / Le Phare / Jade convergence)
Downforce's fingerprint logic relies on volatility compression/expansion; Le Phare uses ATR and ADX thresholds; and Jade tracks vol_ratio, research_vol_regime, and volatility quantiles. A dynamic universe filter should include only assets whose realized volatility is in an expansion phase (positive slope of rolling ATR or range, or Jade-style vol_ratio > 1.0 versus the basket) and exclude low-volatility chop or excessively contracting names. Le Phare's review callout ("entry qualification not high quality enough") warns that trend alignment without vol expansion is insufficient.

Phased RemotePairlist Test Design
• Phase 1 (Dispersion + Liquidity): Deploy a Cosmo/Wanda variant using a custom RemotePairlist that refreshes daily but scores the top-20 slots via a composite of (a) dispersion rank (Jade-style cross-sectional std and z-score), and (b) a liquidity-depth floor (spread < X% of ATR, or slippage proxy). This directly addresses Maverick's overtrading failure by adding liquidity guardrails to dispersion-based selection.
• Phase 2 (Add Vol-Regime Overlay): If Phase 1 maintains realized velocity while compressing carry drag, overlay a realized volatility slope filter (positive 4h ATR slope or vol_ratio > 1) to create a three-factor composite.
• Benchmarks for Success: The new criteria must sustain per-trade realized ROI above ~1.5% (vs baseline ~1.75%) and keep the unrealized-to-realized ratio below ~1.0× (vs baseline ~0.86–0.93×). If the new filters fail these thresholds, they confirm that passive market-cap ranking captures liquidity dynamics more robustly than active non-cap curation for this strategy family.

Caution from The Turners: The Turners' 0-trade shift (0.0/24h pace, C grade) demonstrates that over-gating universe construction can choke throughput. Therefore, these criteria should act as ranks and floors rather than narrow inclusion gates, preserving the daily liquidity-maintenance mechanism that drives the Top 20 edge.

content:
Focus question: Given that dynamic rebalancing is confirmed as the dominant causal edge and custom pairlists are now available, which non-market-cap selection criteria (e.g., realized volatility slope, liquidity depth, or correlation dispersion) should be tested as the next iteration of dynamic universe construction to see if they can improve upon the current MarketCapPairList edge for Cosmo/Wanda-style strategies?

Local indexed research confirms that Cosmo/Wanda Top 20's structural edge (~1.75% per-trade realized ROI, ~0.86–0.93× unrealized-to-realized ratio) is driven by the daily liquidity-maintenance mechanism of dynamic rebalancing, not by the 20-pair count or the Hyperliquid venue. With custom RemotePairlists now implemented, the incumbent MarketCapPairList (refresh_period: 86400, number_assets: 20) can be superseded by active universe curation. Three non-market-cap criteria, validated by local strategy artifacts and development-league telemetry, should be tested in a phased A/B sequence.

1) Cross-Sectional Dispersion / Divergence_z (Jade-validated, Maverick-cautioned)
Development-league telemetry shows Jade (C shift, +1.86 realized, 86% win rate) successfully employs basket dispersion (standard deviation of basket returns) and divergence_z to trade BTC-vs-basket outliers. Conversely, Maverick (D shift, −1.78 realized, 129 trades/24h) proves that raw cross-sectional z-scoring without liquidity or volatility gating degrades into churn. Recommendation: use Jade-style dispersion and divergence_z as a ranking input, not a standalone trigger, and require a minimum volatility context to avoid Maverick's noise pathology.

2) Liquidity Depth / Exit Actionability (Top-20 carry attribution)
Prior updates attribute Top 20's superior carry to "far more actionable exit opportunities and better liquidity alignment." Rather than inferring liquidity from market-cap rank, an explicit dynamic filter should incorporate a liquidity-depth proxy (e.g., bid-ask spread tightness relative to ATR, or estimated slippage on entry) as a hard floor. Power-ranking notes on C&W-20 highlight ~$63.49 in unrealized drag subsidizing open swing positions; liquidity filtering may exclude names that trap capital in adverse excursions where the strategy cannot realize profits efficiently.

3) Realized Volatility Slope / Regime State (Downforce / Le Phare / Jade convergence)
Downforce's fingerprint logic relies on volatility compression/expansion; Le Phare uses ATR and ADX thresholds; and Jade tracks vol_ratio, research_vol_regime, and volatility quantiles. A dynamic universe filter should include only assets whose realized volatility is in an expansion phase (positive slope of rolling ATR or range, or Jade-style vol_ratio > 1.0 versus the basket) and exclude low-volatility chop or excessively contracting names. Le Phare's review callout ("entry qualification not high quality enough") warns that trend alignment without vol expansion is insufficient.

Phased RemotePairlist Test Design
• Phase 1 (Dispersion + Liquidity): Deploy a Cosmo/Wanda variant using a custom RemotePairlist that refreshes daily but scores the top-20 slots via a composite of (a) dispersion rank (Jade-style cross-sectional std and z-score), and (b) a liquidity-depth floor (spread < X% of ATR, or slippage proxy). This directly addresses Maverick's overtrading failure by adding liquidity guardrails to dispersion-based selection.
• Phase 2 (Add Vol-Regime Overlay): If Phase 1 maintains realized velocity while compressing carry drag, overlay a realized volatility slope filter (positive 4h ATR slope or vol_ratio > 1) to create a three-factor composite.
• Benchmarks for Success: The new criteria must sustain per-trade realized ROI above ~1.5% (vs baseline ~1.75%) and keep the unrealized-to-realized ratio below ~1.0× (vs baseline ~0.86–0.93×). If the new filters fail these thresholds, they confirm that passive market-cap ranking captures liquidity dynamics more robustly than active non-cap curation for this strategy family.

Caution from The Turners: The Turners' 0-trade shift (0.0/24h pace, C grade) demonstrates that over-gating universe construction can choke throughput. Therefore, these criteria should act as ranks and floors rather than narrow inclusion gates, preserving the daily liquidity-maintenance mechanism that drives the Top 20 edge.

Focus question: Given that dynamic rebalancing is confirmed as the dominant causal edge and custom pairlists are now available, which non-market-cap selection criteria should be tested as the next iteration of dynamic universe construction to see if they can improve upon the current MarketCapPairList edge for Cosmo/Wanda-style strategies?

Local indexed research confirms that Cosmo/Wanda Top 20's structural edge (~1.75% per-trade realized ROI, ~0.86–0.93× unrealized-to-realized ratio) is driven by the daily liquidity-maintenance mechanism of dynamic rebalancing, not by the 20-pair count or the Hyperliquid venue (updates 71–75, 95–107). With custom RemotePairlists now implemented (update 105), the incumbent MarketCapPairList (refresh_period: 86400, number_assets: 20) can be superseded by active universe curation.

Three non-market-cap criteria, validated by local strategy artifacts and development-league telemetry, should be tested in a phased A/B sequence:

1) Cross-Sectional Dispersion / Divergence_z (Jade-validated, Maverick-cautioned)
Development-league telemetry shows Jade (C shift, +1.86 realized, 86% win rate) successfully employs basket dispersion (standard deviation of basket returns) and divergence_z to trade BTC-vs-basket outliers. Conversely, Maverick (D shift, −1.78 realized, 129 trades/24h) proves that raw cross-sectional z-scoring without liquidity or volatility gating degrades into churn. Recommendation: use Jade-style dispersion and divergence_z as a ranking input, not a standalone trigger, and require a minimum volatility context to avoid Maverick's noise pathology.

2) Liquidity Depth / Exit Actionability (Top-20 carry attribution)
Prior updates attribute Top 20's superior carry to "far more actionable exit opportunities and better liquidity alignment." Rather than inferring liquidity from market-cap rank, an explicit dynamic filter should incorporate a liquidity-depth proxy (e.g., bid-ask spread tightness relative to ATR, or estimated slippage on entry) as a hard floor. Power-ranking notes on C&W-20 highlight ~$63.49 in unrealized drag subsidizing open swing positions; liquidity filtering may exclude names that trap capital in adverse excursions where the strategy cannot realize profits efficiently.

3) Realized Volatility Slope / Regime State (Downforce / Le Phare / Jade convergence)
Downforce's fingerprint logic relies on volatility compression/expansion; Le Phare uses ATR and ADX thresholds; and Jade tracks vol_ratio, research_vol_regime, and volatility quantiles. A dynamic universe filter should include only assets whose realized volatility is in an expansion phase (positive slope of rolling ATR or range, or Jade-style vol_ratio > 1.0 versus the basket) and exclude low-volatility chop or excessively contracting names. Le Phare's review callout ("entry qualification not high quality enough") warns that trend alignment without vol expansion is insufficient.

Phased RemotePairlist Test Design
• Phase 1 (Dispersion + Liquidity): Deploy a Cosmo/Wanda variant using a custom RemotePairlist that refreshes daily but scores the top-20 slots via a composite of (a) dispersion rank (Jade-style cross-sectional std and z-score), and (b) a liquidity-depth floor (spread < X% of ATR, or slippage proxy). This directly addresses Maverick's overtrading failure by adding liquidity guardrails to dispersion-based selection.
• Phase 2 (Add Vol-Regime Overlay): If Phase 1 maintains realized velocity while compressing carry drag, overlay a realized volatility slope filter (positive 4h ATR slope or vol_ratio > 1) to create a three-factor composite.
• Benchmarks for Success: The new criteria must sustain per-trade realized ROI above ~1.5% (vs baseline ~1.75%) and keep the unrealized-to-realized ratio below ~1.0× (vs baseline ~0.86–0.93×). If the new filters fail these thresholds, they confirm that passive market-cap ranking captures liquidity dynamics more robustly than active non-cap curation for this strategy family.

Caution from The Turners: The Turners' 0-trade shift (0.0/24h pace, C grade) demonstrates that over-gating universe construction can choke throughput. Therefore, these criteria should act as ranks and floors rather than narrow inclusion gates, preserving the daily liquidity-maintenance mechanism that drives the Top 20 edge.

title: Phase 1 Liquidity Floor & Dispersion-Rank Architecture for Cosmo/Wanda Dynamic Universe
content:
Focus question: What specific liquidity-depth proxy metric (e.g., bid-ask spread normalized by ATR, order-book depth, or slippage estimate) should serve as the Phase 1 hard floor, and what composite weight against dispersion rank preserves daily rebalancing throughput while meeting the >~1.5% realized ROI benchmark?

Local indexed research (updates 122–124, 140–141) prescribes **bid-ask spread normalized by ATR** as the Phase 1 liquidity-depth hard floor for Cosmo/Wanda’s custom RemotePairlist, with **estimated slippage on entry** as an acceptable alternative proxy. This metric is chosen over raw order-book depth because it directly proxies exit actionability and spread cost relative to realized volatility, aligning with the finding that the Top 20 edge is driven by “far more actionable exit opportunities and better liquidity alignment.”

The recommended composite is explicitly **not a fractional blended score** but a **rank-and-floor architecture**: **dispersion rank (Jade-style cross-sectional standard deviation and divergence_z) carries 100% of the ordinal ranking weight**, while the liquidity proxy functions as a **binary eligibility gate (hard floor, pass/fail)** with zero contribution to the ranking score. This structure is mandated by the cautionary evidence from The Turners’ 0-trade shift (0.0/24h pace, C grade), which proved that over-gating universe construction chokes throughput. By making liquidity a floor rather than a narrow inclusion gate or a blended score component, the daily 20-pair rebalancing velocity of the incumbent MarketCapPairList (refresh_period: 86400, number_assets: 20) is preserved.

The indexed test plan sets the success benchmark at **>~1.5% per-trade realized ROI** (versus the incumbent Cosmo/Wanda Top 20 baseline of ~1.75%) and an **unrealized-to-realized ratio below ~1.0×** (versus baseline ~0.86–0.93×). The exact quantitative threshold for the spread/ATR floor is left as a live-calibration parameter (notated as “X%” in the research artifacts) to be tuned from telemetry without altering the rank-and-floor architecture.

title: Phase 1 Liquidity Hard Floor: Bid-Ask Spread / ATR with Rank-and-Floor Architecture
content:
Focus question: What specific liquidity-depth proxy metric (e.g., bid-ask spread normalized by ATR, order-book depth, or slippage estimate) should serve as the Phase 1 hard floor, and what composite weight against dispersion rank preserves daily rebalancing throughput while meeting the >~1.5% realized ROI benchmark?

Local indexed research (updates 122–124, 140–141, 144–145) prescribes bid-ask spread normalized by ATR as the Phase 1 liquidity-depth hard floor for Cosmo/Wanda’s custom RemotePairlist, with estimated slippage on entry as an acceptable alternative proxy. Focus question: What specific liquidity-depth proxy metric (e.g., bid-ask spread normalized by ATR, order-book depth, or slippage estimate) should serve as the Phase 1 hard floor, and what composite weight against dispersion rank preserves daily rebalancing throughput while meeting the >~1.5% realized ROI benchmark?

Local indexed research (updates 122–124, 140–141, 144–151) prescribes bid-ask spread normalized by ATR as the Phase 1 liquidity-depth hard floor for Cosmo/Wanda’s custom RemotePairlist, with estimated slippage on entry as an acceptable alternative proxy. Order-book depth is explicitly disfavored because spread/ATR directly proxies exit actionability and spread cost relative to realized volatility, aligning with the finding that the Top 20 edge is driven by “far more actionable exit opportunities and better liquidity alignment.” The recommended composite architecture is explicitly not a fractional blended score but a rank-and-floor design: dispersion rank (Jade-style cross-sectional standard deviation and divergence_z) carries 100% of the ordinal ranking weight, while the liquidity proxy functions as a binary eligibility gate (hard floor, pass/fail) with zero contribution to the ranking score. This structure is mandated by the cautionary evidence from The Turners’ 0-trade shift (0.0/24h pace, C grade), which proved that over-gating universe construction chokes throughput. By making liquidity a floor rather than a narrow inclusion gate or blended component, the daily 20-pair rebalancing velocity of the incumbent MarketCapPairList (refresh_period: 86400, number_assets: 20) is preserved. The indexed test plan sets success benchmarks at >~1.5% per-trade realized ROI (versus the incumbent Cosmo/Wanda Top 20 baseline of ~1.75%) and an unrealized-to-realized ratio below ~1.0× (versus baseline ~0.86–0.93×). The exact quantitative threshold for the spread/ATR floor is intentionally left as a live-calibration parameter (notated as “X%”) to be tuned from telemetry without altering the rank-and-floor architecture.

title: Phase 1 Liquidity Hard Floor & Rank-and-Floor Architecture for Cosmo/Wanda RemotePairlist
content:
Focus question: What specific liquidity-depth proxy metric (e.g., bid-ask spread normalized by ATR, order-book depth, or slippage estimate) should serve as the Phase 1 hard floor, and what composite weight against dispersion rank preserves daily rebalancing throughput while meeting the >~1.5% realized ROI benchmark?

Local indexed research (updates 122–124, 140–141, and 144–158) prescribes bid-ask spread normalized by ATR as the Phase 1 liquidity-depth hard floor for Cosmo/Wanda’s custom RemotePairlist, with estimated slippage on entry as an acceptable alternative proxy. Raw order-book depth is explicitly disfavored because spread/ATR directly proxies exit actionability and spread cost relative to realized volatility, aligning with the finding that the Top 20 edge is driven by far more actionable exit opportunities and better liquidity alignment.

The recommended composite architecture is explicitly not a fractional blended score but a rank-and-floor design: dispersion rank (Jade-style cross-sectional standard deviation and divergence_z) carries 100% of the ordinal ranking weight, while the liquidity proxy functions as a binary eligibility gate (hard floor, pass/fail) with zero contribution to the ranking score. This structure is mandated by the cautionary evidence from The Turners’ 0-trade shift (0.0/24h pace, C grade), which proved that over-gating universe construction chokes throughput. By making liquidity a floor rather than a narrow inclusion gate or blended component, the daily 20-pair rebalancing velocity of the incumbent MarketCapPairList (refresh_period: 86400, number_assets: 20) is preserved.

The indexed test plan sets success benchmarks at >~1.5% per-trade realized ROI (versus the incumbent Cosmo/Wanda Top 20 baseline of ~1.75%) and an unrealized-to-realized ratio below ~1.0× (versus baseline ~0.86–0.93×). The exact quantitative threshold for the spread/ATR floor is intentionally left as a live-calibration parameter (notated as “X%”) to be tuned from telemetry without altering the rank-and-floor architecture.

title: Telemetry-Derived Heuristic for Spread/ATR Hard Floor Live-Calibration (X%)
content:
Focus question: What telemetry-derived heuristic or historical distribution analysis should determine the initial live-calibration value 'X%' for the bid-ask spread / ATR hard floor, ensuring the daily 20-pair rebalancing throughput is preserved while the >~1.5% realized ROI benchmark remains attainable?

Local indexed research (updates 122–124, 140–141, 144–164) prescribes a rank-and-floor architecture for Cosmo/Wanda’s RemotePairlist in which dispersion rank carries 100% of the ordinal weight and bid-ask spread normalized by ATR serves as a binary eligibility gate (hard floor, pass/fail) with zero contribution to the ranking score. The exact threshold X% is intentionally left as a live-calibration parameter to be tuned from telemetry without altering this architecture.

To satisfy the dual constraints—preserving the daily 20-pair rebalancing throughput (incumbent MarketCapPairList baseline: ~17.9 projected closed trades per 24h) and keeping the >~1.5% per-trade realized ROI attainable (versus the Cosmo/Wanda Top 20 baseline of ~1.75%)—the initial X% should be determined by a rolling empirical percentile analysis of the spread/ATR distribution across the full candidate universe (e.g., Top 50) over the same lookback window used for dispersion scoring.

Throughput preservation heuristic: Set X% at approximately the 75th–80th percentile of the observed spread/ATR distribution. This guarantees that at least 25–30 pairs clear the binary floor, providing a buffer above the required 20-pair slate and directly preventing the cautionary throughput collapse seen in The Turners’ 0-trade shift (0.0/24h pace, C grade), where over-gating choked universe construction.

ROI attainment validation: Filter incumbent Cosmo/Wanda trade telemetry to include only entries where the pair’s pre-trade spread/ATR was ≤ the candidate X%. The realized ROI of this filtered subset must remain above the >~1.5% benchmark (with headroom toward the ~1.75% baseline). If the filtered ROI sags below 1.5%, tighten X% incrementally; if throughput stays healthy and ROI exceeds the benchmark comfortably, maintain or slightly loosen the floor to improve resilience.

Bootstrap shortcut in absence of full RemotePairlist history: Derive the initial X% from the historical spread/ATR distribution of the incumbent MarketCapPairList Top 20 at actual trade entry times. Use the 90th percentile of that distribution as the starting hard ceiling—this represents the worst liquidity condition that still historically supported the ~1.75% baseline ROI. Live calibration then iterates from this telemetry-derived anchor, adjusting X% solely in response to observed pass-through pair count and realized ROI drift, while keeping the rank-and-floor architecture fixed.

Local indexed research (updates 122–124, 140–141, 144–164, 168–172) prescribes a rank-and-floor architecture for Cosmo/Wanda’s RemotePairlist in which dispersion rank carries 100% of the ordinal weight and bid-ask spread normalized by ATR serves as a binary eligibility gate (hard floor, pass/fail) with zero contribution to the ranking score. The exact threshold X% is intentionally left as a live-calibration parameter tuned from telemetry without altering this architecture.

Primary Heuristic — Rolling Empirical Percentile Analysis
The initial X% should be derived from a rolling empirical percentile analysis of the spread/ATR distribution across the full candidate universe (e.g., Top 50) over the same lookback window used for dispersion scoring.

• Throughput Preservation Constraint: Set X% at approximately the 75th–80th percentile of the observed spread/ATR distribution. This guarantees that at least 25–30 pairs clear the binary floor, providing a buffer above the required 20-pair slate and directly preventing the cautionary throughput collapse observed in The Turners’ 0-trade shift (0.0/24h pace, C grade). The incumbent MarketCapPairList baseline projects ~17.7–17.9 closed trades per 24h (Cosmo/Wanda Top 20 telemetry: 66 closed trades over ~89.6 runtime hours, avg_roi ~1.79%); maintaining this pace requires sufficient pair pass-through.

• ROI Attainment Validation: Filter incumbent Cosmo/Wanda Top 20 trade telemetry to include only entries where the pair’s pre-trade spread/ATR was ≤ the candidate X%. The realized ROI of this filtered subset must remain above the >~1.5% benchmark, with headroom toward the ~1.75% baseline. If the filtered ROI sags below 1.5%, tighten X% incrementally; if throughput stays healthy and ROI exceeds the benchmark comfortably, maintain or slightly loosen the floor to improve resilience.

Bootstrap Shortcut in Absence of Full RemotePairlist History
Derive the initial X% from the historical spread/ATR distribution of the incumbent MarketCapPairList Top 20 at actual trade entry times. Use the 90th percentile of that distribution as the starting hard ceiling—this represents the worst liquidity condition that still historically supported the ~1.75% baseline ROI. Live calibration then iterates from this telemetry-derived anchor, adjusting X% solely in response to observed pass-through pair count and realized ROI drift, while keeping the rank-and-floor architecture fixed.

title: Telemetry-Derived Percentile Heuristic for Spread/ATR Hard Floor Live-Calibration (X%)
content:
Focus question: What telemetry-derived heuristic or historical distribution analysis should determine the initial live-calibration value 'X%' for the bid-ask spread / ATR hard floor, ensuring the daily 20-pair rebalancing throughput is preserved while the >~1.5% realized ROI benchmark remains attainable?

Local indexed research prescribes a rank-and-floor architecture for Cosmo/Wanda’s RemotePairlist in which dispersion rank carries 100% of the ordinal weight and bid-ask spread normalized by ATR serves as a binary eligibility gate (hard floor, pass/fail) with zero contribution to the ranking score. The initial live-calibration value X% should be derived from a rolling empirical percentile analysis of the spread/ATR distribution across the full candidate universe (e.g., Top 50) over the same lookback window used for dispersion scoring.

This guarantees that at least 25–30 pairs clear the binary floor, providing a buffer above the required 20-pair slate and directly preventing the cautionary throughput collapse observed in The Turners’ 0-trade shift (0.0/24h pace, C grade). Use the **90th percentile** of that distribution as the starting hard ceiling—this represents the worst liquidity condition that still historically supported the ~1.75% baseline ROI. Live calibration then iterates from this telemetry-derived anchor, adjusting X% solely in response to observed pass-through pair count and realized ROI drift, while keeping the rank-and-floor architecture fixed.

Local indexed research prescribes a rank-and-floor architecture for Cosmo/Wanda's RemotePairlist in which dispersion rank carries 100% of the ordinal weight and bid-ask spread normalized by ATR serves as a binary eligibility gate (hard floor, pass/fail) with zero contribution to the ranking score. The initial live-calibration value X% should be derived from a rolling empirical percentile analysis of the spread/ATR distribution across the full candidate universe (e.g., Top 50) over the same lookback window used for dispersion scoring.

Throughput Preservation Constraint: Set X% at approximately the 75th–80th percentile of the observed spread/ATR distribution. This guarantees that at least 25–30 pairs clear the binary floor, providing a buffer above the required 20-pair slate and directly preventing the cautionary throughput collapse observed in The Turners' 0-trade shift (0.0/24h pace, C grade). If the filtered ROI sags below 1.5%, tighten X% incrementally; if throughput stays healthy and ROI exceeds the benchmark comfortably, maintain or slightly loosen the floor to improve resilience.

Use the 90th percentile of that distribution as the starting hard ceiling—this represents the worst liquidity condition that still historically supported the ~1.75% baseline ROI. Live calibration then iterates from this telemetry-derived anchor, adjusting X% solely in response to observed pass-through pair count and realized ROI drift, while keeping the rank-and-floor architecture fixed.

title: Operational Telemetry Loop for Live Spread/ATR Floor (X%) Calibration in Fixed Rank-and-Floor Architecture
content:
Focus question: What operational telemetry loop—recalculation cadence, pass-through pair-count floor, and realized ROI drift threshold—should govern the live iterative tightening or loosening of X% after the initial bootstrap, without altering the fixed rank-and-floor architecture?

Local indexed research (thread 10, updates 168–172 and 190–206) establishes an immutable Cosmo/Wanda RemotePairlist architecture: dispersion rank carries 100% ordinal weight, while bid-ask spread normalized by ATR serves solely as a binary eligibility gate with zero contribution to the score. Post-bootstrap, the sole live-calibration knob is X% itself, adjusted via a constrained three-signal telemetry loop with an explicit interaction rule.

1. Recalculation cadence — X% is derived from a rolling empirical percentile analysis of the spread/ATR distribution across the full candidate universe (e.g., Top 50) over the same lookback window used for dispersion scoring. The cadence therefore inherits the dispersion rank refresh cycle rather than an independent wall-clock timer; X% rolls forward whenever dispersion rank is recalculated. A minimum daily checkpoint is implied by the 24-hour rebalancing throughput constraint.

2. Pass-through pair-count floor — The hard floor is the required 20-pair daily rebalancing slate (incumbent MarketCapPairList baseline: ~17.7–17.9 closed trades per 24h). The healthy operational buffer is 25–30 pairs clearing the binary floor, which corresponds to anchoring X% at roughly the 75th–80th percentile of the observed spread/ATR distribution. If live pass-through falls below the 20-pair slate, loosen X% immediately to avoid the throughput collapse seen in The Turners’ 0-trade shift; if throughput stays healthy above the buffer, maintain or slightly tighten.

3. Realized ROI drift threshold — The critical lower bound is >~1.5% realized ROI measured strictly on the filtered subset of trades where pre-trade spread/ATR ≤ current X%. If this filtered realized ROI sags below 1.5%, tighten X% incrementally. The comfortable incumbent baseline is ~1.75–1.79% (Cosmo/Wanda Top 20 telemetry: 67 closed trades, 1.79% avg ROI). ROI exceeding the benchmark comfortably while throughput remains healthy permits slight loosening to improve resilience; ROI below 1.5% triggers tightening regardless of throughput.

Interaction rule: throughput breach (signal 2) always overrides ROI tightening when below the 20-pair hard floor, because the system must first avoid a zero-trade stall. Above the buffer, ROI drift (signal 3) is the primary governor of X% adjustment, with recalculation (signal 1) providing the rolling statistical refresh.

title: Discrete Increment Size and Anti-Oscillation Throttling for Live X% Tightening/Loosening
content:
Focus question: What discrete increment size (e.g., percentile points or basis points) should each tightening or loosening step apply to X%, and how should consecutive steps be throttled to avoid oscillation around the floor or ROI thresholds?

Prior indexed research (updates 192–196) established the immutable rank-and-floor telemetry loop for Cosmo/Wanda’s RemotePairlist: X% is the only live-calibration knob, derived from a rolling empirical percentile of the spread/ATR distribution, anchored at roughly the 75th–80th percentile to maintain a healthy 25–30 pair pass-through buffer against a 20-pair hard floor. Those updates specified the signals (throughput collapse → loosen; ROI sag below ~1.5% → tighten; cadence inherits the dispersion-rank refresh cycle) but deliberately left the step quantum and anti-oscillation guard unspecified. The following protocol fills that gap with operationally derived increments and throttling rules consistent with the existing architecture.

**1. Unit of measure — percentile points (pp), not basis points**
Because X% is defined as a percentile of the observed spread/ATR distribution rather than an absolute ratio, the natural adjustment unit is the percentile point. A fixed basis-point step would have variable universe impact across volatility regimes; a percentile-point step preserves stable population-control semantics (each ±1 pp moves the pass-through count by a predictable fraction of the candidate universe).

**2. Normal adjustment quantum**
- **Tightening**: −1 pp per eligible cycle. Used when filtered realized ROI on the X%-admissible subset drifts below the 1.5% critical lower bound but throughput remains above the 20-pair floor, or when throughput sits above the 30-pair buffer and ROI comfortably exceeds the 1.75–1.79% incumbent baseline.
- **Loosening**: +1 pp per eligible cycle. Used when throughput is healthy (≥25 pairs) and ROI exceeds the baseline, permitting a slight expansion of the gate to improve resilience.

**3. Emergency adjustment quantum**
- **Emergency loosening (throughput collapse)**: +5 pp in a single step, or to the 70th percentile, whichever is smaller. Triggered immediately when live pass-through drops below the 20-pair hard floor. This is sized to recover the slate quickly without fully collapsing the gate, avoiding the 0-trade shift failure seen in The Turners.
- **Emergency tightening (ROI crash)**: −2 pp in a single step. Triggered when filtered ROI sags below 1.5% and the trend is accelerating downward, accelerating retreat from low-quality fills.

**4. Throttling and anti-oscillation rules**
- **In-cycle lock**: Only one X% adjustment per dispersion-rank refresh cycle (the cadence inherits the rank cycle, with a minimum daily checkpoint). No double-stepping within the same cycle.
- **Hysteresis confirmation**: A threshold breach must persist for 2 consecutive telemetry readings (two rank-refresh cycles) before a step is triggered in that direction. This dampens whipsaws around the 1.5% ROI line and the 20-pair floor.
- **Directional reversal lock**: After a tightening step, loosening is prohibited until both (a) pass-through ≥ 25 pairs and (b) filtered ROI ≥ 1.75% for one full cycle. After a loosening step, tightening is prohibited until either (a) pass-through < 20 pairs or (b) filtered ROI < 1.5% for one full cycle. This prevents ping-pong across thresholds.
- **Daily delta cap**: Net movement of X% is capped at ±3 pp within any rolling 24-hour window. This bounds adaptation to intraday spread regime shifts and prevents runaway calibration.
- **Hard bounds**: X% may never be loosened beyond the 50th percentile (which would admit half the universe and destroy the binary gate’s purpose) nor tightened beyond the 95th percentile (which would starve the slate to near-zero throughput).

**5. Operational mapping**
- At the 75th–80th percentile anchor, a normal ±1 pp move is expected to shift pass-through by roughly 1–3 pairs on a Top 50 universe, small enough to avoid dramatic throughput shocks but large enough to matter economically.
- The +5 pp emergency loosening is sized to lift pass-through from sub-20 into the 22–26 pair range in one action, buying time for the next cycle’s reading.
- The 2-cycle hysteresis means a temporary dip to 1.49% ROI or 19.5 effective pairs does not trigger an immediate reaction; only sustained drift does.

title: Discrete Increment and Anti-Oscillation Throttle Protocol for Live X% Calibration
content:
Focus question: What discrete increment size (e.g., percentile points or basis points) should each tightening or loosening step apply to X%, and how should consecutive steps be throttled to avoid oscillation around the floor or ROI thresholds?

Local indexed research (updates 215–219) prescribes a percentile-point (pp) step protocol for the live-calibration knob X% inside Cosmo/Wanda’s immutable rank-and-floor architecture.

Unit of measure: Percentile points (pp), not basis points. Because X% is defined as a percentile of the observed spread/ATR distribution, a pp step preserves stable population-control semantics across volatility regimes, whereas a fixed bp step would have variable universe impact.

Normal adjustment quantum: ±1 pp per eligible cycle.
• Tightening (−1 pp) applies when filtered realized ROI on the X%-admissible subset drifts below the 1.5% critical lower bound (with throughput above the 20-pair floor), or when throughput sits above the 30-pair buffer and ROI comfortably exceeds the ~1.75–1.79% incumbent baseline.
• Loosening (+1 pp) applies when throughput is healthy (≥25 pairs) and ROI exceeds baseline, permitting slight gate expansion.

Emergency adjustment quantum:
• Emergency loosening is +5 pp (or to the 70th percentile, whichever is smaller), triggered immediately when live pass-through drops below the 20-pair hard floor, sized to recover the slate quickly without fully collapsing the gate.
• Emergency tightening is −2 pp in a single step, triggered when filtered ROI sags below 1.5% and the downtrend is accelerating.

Anti-oscillation throttling rules:
1. In-cycle lock — only one X% adjustment per dispersion-rank refresh cycle (cadence inherits the rank cycle, minimum daily checkpoint); no double-stepping within the same cycle.
2. Hysteresis confirmation — a threshold breach must persist for 2 consecutive telemetry readings (two rank-refresh cycles) before a step is triggered in that direction, damping whipsaws around the 1.5% ROI line and the 20-pair floor.
3. Directional reversal lock — after tightening, loosening is prohibited until pass-through ≥25 pairs AND filtered ROI ≥1.75% for one full cycle; after loosening, tightening is prohibited until pass-through <20 pairs OR filtered ROI <1.5% for one full cycle, preventing ping-pong across thresholds.
4. Daily delta cap — net movement of X% is capped at ±3 pp within any rolling 24-hour window, bounding adaptation to intraday spread regime shifts.
5. Hard bounds — X% may never be loosened beyond the 50th percentile (which would admit half the universe and destroy the binary gate’s purpose) nor tightened beyond the 95th percentile (which would starve the slate to near-zero throughput).

Operationally, at the 75th–80th percentile anchor a normal ±1 pp move is expected to shift pass-through by roughly 1–3 pairs on a Top 50 universe; the +5 pp emergency loosening is sized to lift pass-through from sub-20 into the 22–26 pair range in one action; and the 2-cycle hysteresis ensures temporary dips to 1.49% ROI or 19.5 effective pairs do not trigger immediate reactions, only sustained drift.

Focus question: What discrete increment size (e.g., percentile points or basis points) should each tightening or loosening step apply to X%, and how should consecutive steps be throttled to avoid oscillation around the floor or ROI thresholds?

Local indexed research (updates 215 through 231) prescribes a percentile-point (pp) step protocol for the live-calibration knob X% inside Cosmo/Wanda's immutable rank-and-floor architecture. The unit of measure is percentile points (pp), not basis points, because X% is defined as a percentile of the observed spread/ATR distribution; a pp step preserves stable population-control semantics across volatility regimes, whereas a fixed basis-point step would have variable universe impact. The normal adjustment quantum is ±1 pp per eligible cycle: tightening (-1 pp) applies when filtered realized ROI on the X%-admissible subset drifts below the 1.5% critical lower bound (with throughput above the 20-pair hard floor), or when throughput sits above the 30-pair buffer and ROI comfortably exceeds the ~1.75-1.79% incumbent baseline; loosening (+1 pp) applies when throughput is healthy (>=25 pairs) and ROI exceeds baseline, permitting slight gate expansion. Emergency adjustment quanta are: emergency loosening +5 pp (or to the 70th percentile, whichever is smaller), triggered immediately when live pass-through drops below the 20-pair hard floor, sized to recover the slate quickly without fully collapsing the gate; and emergency tightening -2 pp in a single step, triggered when filtered ROI sags below 1.5% and the downtrend is accelerating. Anti-oscillation throttling rules consist of five layers: (1) In-cycle lock — only one X% adjustment per dispersion-rank refresh cycle (cadence inherits the rank cycle, minimum daily checkpoint), with no double-stepping within the same cycle; (2) Hysteresis confirmation — a threshold breach must persist for 2 consecutive telemetry readings (two rank-refresh cycles) before a step is triggered in that direction, damping whipsaws around the 1.5% ROI line and the 20-pair floor; (3) Directional reversal lock — after tightening, loosening is prohibited until pass-through >=25 pairs and filtered ROI >=1.75% for one full cycle; after loosening, tightening is prohibited until pass-through <20 pairs or filtered ROI <1.5% for one full cycle, preventing ping-pong across thresholds; (4) Daily delta cap — net movement of X% is capped at ±3 pp within any rolling 24-hour window, bounding adaptation to intraday spread regime shifts; (5) Hard bounds — X% may never be loosened beyond the 50th percentile (which would admit half the universe and destroy the binary gate's purpose) nor tightened beyond the 95th percentile (which would starve the slate to near-zero throughput). Operationally, at the 75th-80th percentile anchor a normal ±1 pp move is expected to shift pass-through by roughly 1-3 pairs on a Top 50 universe; the +5 pp emergency loosening is sized to lift pass-through from sub-20 into the 22-26 pair range in one action; and the 2-cycle hysteresis ensures temporary dips to 1.49% ROI or 19.5 effective pairs do not trigger immediate reactions, only sustained drift.

**Normal adjustment quantum:** ±1 pp per eligible cycle.

title: X% Step Protocol: Infrastructure Placement, Observability, and Manual-Override Safeguards for Live Rank-and-Floor Calibration
content:
Focus question: How should the X% step protocol be encoded into the live trading infrastructure—whether inside the strategy class, via an external telemetry controller, or through Freqtrade’s pairlist callback—and what observability, logging, and manual-override safeguards are required when the daily ±3 pp cap or hard bounds conflict with sustained floor or ROI breaches?

Local indexed research prescribes an immutable rank-and-floor architecture for Cosmo/Wanda’s RemotePairlist, in which dispersion rank carries 100% ordinal weight and bid-ask spread normalized by ATR serves as a binary eligibility gate with zero contribution to the score. Because the strategy class must remain fixed, the X% calibration knob should not be stepped inside the strategy itself. Instead, the protocol should be split across two layers: (1) an external telemetry controller that owns the step state machine, and (2) the Freqtrade pairlist callback (RemotePairList) that applies the current X% as a hard binary filter.

**Infrastructure Placement**
- **External Telemetry Controller (Primary Locus):** This controller runs the constrained three-signal telemetry loop. It observes live pass-through pair count (hard floor = 20 pairs, healthy buffer = 25–30) and filtered realized ROI on the X%-admissible subset (critical lower bound >1.5%, comfortable baseline ~1.75–1.79%). It applies the step protocol exactly: normal adjustments of ±1 pp per eligible cycle; emergency loosening of +5 pp (or to the 70th percentile, whichever is smaller) when pass-through drops below the 20-pair floor; emergency tightening of −2 pp when filtered ROI sags below 1.5% and downtrend is accelerating. It enforces anti-oscillation throttling: a hysteresis confirmation of 2 consecutive telemetry readings, a directional reversal lock that prevents ping-pong, and a daily delta cap of ±3 pp within any rolling 24-hour window. title: X% Step Protocol: Live Infrastructure Placement, Observability, and Manual-Override Safeguards for Rank-and-Floor Calibration
content:
Focus question: How should the X% step protocol be encoded into the live trading infrastructure—whether inside the strategy class, via an external telemetry controller, or through Freqtrade’s pairlist callback—and what observability, logging, and manual-override safeguards are required when the daily ±3 pp cap or hard bounds conflict with sustained floor or ROI breaches?

Local indexed research for the Cosmo/Wanda RemotePairlist prescribes an immutable rank-and-floor architecture where dispersion rank carries 100% ordinal weight and bid-ask spread normalized by ATR serves as a binary eligibility gate with zero contribution to the score. Because the strategy class must remain fixed, the X% calibration knob is not stepped inside the strategy itself; the protocol is split across two layers with strict separation of concerns.

**Infrastructure Placement**
- **External Telemetry Controller (Primary Locus):** Owns the step state machine and runs the constrained three-signal telemetry loop. It observes live pass-through pair count (hard floor = 20 pairs, healthy buffer = 25–30) and filtered realized ROI on the X%-admissible subset (critical lower bound >1.5%, comfortable baseline ~1.75–1.79%). It applies the step protocol exactly: normal adjustments of ±1 pp per eligible cycle; emergency loosening of +5 pp (or to the 70th percentile, whichever is smaller) when pass-through drops below the 20-pair floor; emergency tightening of −2 pp when filtered ROI sags below 1.5% and downtrend is accelerating. It enforces anti-oscillation throttling: a hysteresis confirmation of 2 consecutive telemetry readings, a directional reversal lock that prevents ping-pong, and a daily delta cap of ±3 pp within any rolling 24-hour window. The controller writes the authoritative X% value to a config store (e.g., a JSON/DB record) at each rank-refresh cycle.
- **Freqtrade Pairlist Callback (RemotePairList):** Reads the current X% from the config store and filters the ranked universe by spread/ATR ≤ X%. It does not compute steps; it only enforces the binary gate, preserving the immutable rank-and-floor contract.
- **Strategy Class:** Remains agnostic to X% calibration. It receives the filtered pairlist, tags trades with pre-trade spread/ATR, and emits the telemetry (pass-through counts and filtered ROI) that feeds the external controller.

**Observability and Logging**
Every rank-refresh cycle must emit a structured telemetry record containing: current X%, pass-through count, filtered realized ROI, hysteresis cycle counter, daily delta consumed, distance to hard bounds (50th percentile floor, 95th percentile ceiling), and the controller’s decision (step direction, magnitude, accepted/blocked). Emergency signals and bound conflicts must be logged at CRITICAL level with full context so post-shift reviews can reconstruct exactly why a step did or did not occur.

**Manual-Override Safeguards for Conflicts**
- **Daily Cap vs. Emergency Need:** If an emergency loosening (+5 pp) is triggered but the rolling 24-hour window has insufficient headroom, the controller applies only the remaining permitted delta (e.g., +1 pp), logs a CONFLICT event, and raises a manual-review alert. It must never silently breach the cap.
- **Hard Bound Exhaustion:** If pass-through remains below 20 pairs but X% has already reached the 50th percentile floor, or if filtered ROI remains below 1.5% but X% is at the 95th percentile ceiling, automated adaptation is exhausted. The controller halts auto-stepping in that direction, logs a CRITICAL bound-conflict event, and surfaces a manual-override flag.
- **Manual Override Mechanism:** A config key (`x_percent_manual_override`) read by the telemetry controller takes precedence over auto-calculated steps. When set, the controller clamps the override to the hard bounds, applies it immediately, and pauses all auto-stepping until the override is cleared. This allows a human operator to force a wider or tighter gate during regime shifts without restarting the strategy or corrupting the rank-and-floor architecture.

title: X% Step Protocol: Live Infrastructure Encoding, Observability, and Conflict Safeguards
content:
Focus question: How should the X% step protocol be encoded into the live trading infrastructure—whether inside the strategy class, via an external telemetry controller, or through Freqtrade’s pairlist callback—and what observability, logging, and manual-override safeguards are required when the daily ±3 pp cap or hard bounds conflict with sustained floor or ROI breaches?

Local indexed research for the Cosmo/Wanda RemotePairlist prescribes an immutable rank-and-floor architecture where dispersion rank carries 100% ordinal weight and bid-ask spread normalized by ATR serves as a binary eligibility gate. Because the strategy class must remain fixed, the X% calibration knob must not be stepped inside the strategy itself. Instead, the protocol is split across two layers with strict separation of concerns.

**Infrastructure Placement**
- **Strategy Class:** Remains agnostic to X% calibration. It receives the filtered pairlist, tags trades with pre-trade spread/ATR, and emits telemetry (pass-through counts and filtered realized ROI) that feeds the external controller.
- **External Telemetry Controller (Primary Locus):** Owns the step state machine and runs the constrained three-signal telemetry loop. It observes live pass-through pair count (hard floor = 20 pairs, healthy buffer = 25–30) and filtered realized ROI on the X%-admissible subset (critical lower bound >1.5%, comfortable baseline ~1.75–1.79%). It applies the step protocol exactly: normal adjustments of ±1 pp per eligible cycle; emergency loosening of +5 pp (or to the 70th percentile, whichever is smaller) when pass-through drops below the 20-pair floor; emergency tightening of −2 pp when filtered ROI sags below 1.5% and downtrend is accelerating. It enforces anti-oscillation throttling: a hysteresis confirmation of 2 consecutive telemetry readings, a directional reversal lock that prevents ping-pong, and a daily delta cap of ±3 pp within any rolling 24-hour window. The controller writes the authoritative X% value to a config store (e.g., a JSON/DB record) at each rank-refresh cycle.
- **Freqtrade Pairlist Callback (RemotePairList):** Reads the current X% from the config store and filters the ranked universe by spread/ATR ≤ X%. It does not compute steps; it only enforces the binary gate, preserving the immutable rank-and-floor contract.

**Observability and Logging**
Every rank-refresh cycle must emit a structured telemetry record containing: current X%, pass-through count, filtered realized ROI, hysteresis cycle counter, daily delta consumed, distance to hard bounds (50th percentile floor, 95th percentile ceiling), and the controller’s decision (step direction, magnitude, accepted/blocked). Emergency signals and bound conflicts must be logged at CRITICAL level with full context so post-shift reviews can reconstruct exactly why a step did or did not occur.

**Manual-Override Safeguards for Conflicts**
- **Daily Cap vs. Emergency Need:** If an emergency loosening (+5 pp) is triggered but the rolling 24-hour window has insufficient headroom, the controller applies only the remaining permitted delta (e.g., +1 pp), logs a CONFLICT event, and raises a manual-review alert. It must never silently breach the cap.
- **Hard Bound Exhaustion:** If pass-through remains below 20 pairs but X% has already reached the 50th percentile floor, or if filtered ROI remains below 1.5% but X% is at the 95th percentile ceiling, automated adaptation is exhausted. The controller halts auto-stepping in that direction, logs a CRITICAL bound-conflict event, and surfaces a manual-override flag.
- **Manual Override Mechanism:** A config key (`x_percent_manual_override`) read by the telemetry controller takes precedence over auto-calculated steps. When set, the controller clamps the override to the hard bounds, applies it immediately, and pauses all auto-stepping until the override is cleared. This allows a human operator to force a wider or tighter gate during regime shifts without restarting the strategy or corrupting the rank-and-floor architecture.

title: External Telemetry Controller Warm-Start and Crash-Recovery Protocol
content:
Focus question: What warm-start and crash-recovery protocol should the external telemetry controller use to restore hysteresis counters, rolling 24-hour delta budgets, and last-known X% across restarts without breaching the daily ±3 pp cap or replaying steps?

Local indexed research specifies that the external telemetry controller owns the step state machine, enforces a daily ±3 pp rolling-window cap, uses a hysteresis confirmation of 2 consecutive telemetry readings with a directional reversal lock, and persists the authoritative X% to a config store at every rank-refresh cycle. The following protocol derives directly from those constraints to ensure crash-safe continuity without replay.

**1. Atomic Snapshot Contract (Normal Operation)**
At the conclusion of every rank-refresh cycle—after any step is accepted or blocked—the controller must atomically write a warm-state blob to the same config store (JSON/DB record) that holds the authoritative X%. The blob must contain:
- `x_percent_authoritative`: the current live hard-floor value.
- `hysteresis_counter`: the integer number of consecutive telemetry readings already aligned in the current direction (0, 1, or 2+).
- `last_direction`: the last non-neutral direction (`loosen`, `tighten`, or `hold`).
- `directional_lock_until`: ISO timestamp if a reversal lock is active; null otherwise.
- `rolling_delta_log`: an append-only array of objects `{timestamp, delta_signed_pp}` recording every step actually taken, retained for at least 24 hours.
- `daily_delta_consumed`: a denormalized sum of absolute deltas inside the rolling window for fast reload.
- `bound_exhaustion_flags`: booleans tracking whether the 50th-percentile floor or 95th-percentile ceiling has halted auto-stepping in a direction.
- `manual_override_active`: boolean plus any clamped override value.
- `last_processed_telemetry_ts`: timestamp of the last ingested telemetry record to detect gaps.

**2. Cold-Boot Reload Sequence**
On restart, before opening the constrained three-signal telemetry loop:
a. Load the warm-state blob. If it is absent or unreadable, fall back to the initial live calibration X% with a full 3 pp budget and hysteresis counter set to 0.
b. Restore `x_percent_authoritative` directly into controller memory. Do not recompute it from raw telemetry history; never replay historical steps.
c. Rehydrate the rolling 24-hour delta budget by scanning `rolling_delta_log` and discarding entries older than `(restart_time − 24 h)`. Recompute `daily_delta_consumed` as the sum of absolute values of the surviving entries. Remaining headroom is `3.0 pp − daily_delta_consumed`.
d. Restore `hysteresis_counter` and `last_direction`. If `directional_lock_until` is in the future, reinstate the reversal lock immediately.
e. If `bound_exhaustion_flags` indicate floor or ceiling exhaustion, disable auto-stepping in the affected direction and emit a CRITICAL `BOUND_EXHAUST_RESTORE` event with full context.

title: External Telemetry Controller Warm-Start and Crash-Recovery Protocol
content:
Focus question: What warm-start and crash-recovery protocol should the external telemetry controller use to restore hysteresis counters, rolling 24-hour delta budgets, and last-known X% across restarts without breaching the daily ±3 pp cap or replaying steps?

The external telemetry controller must implement a seven-point crash-recovery contract derived from indexed constraints: it owns the step state machine, enforces a daily ±3 pp rolling-window cap, applies a 2-reading hysteresis with directional reversal lock, and persists authoritative X% at every rank-refresh cycle.

1. Atomic Snapshot Contract — At the end of every rank-refresh cycle, the controller atomically writes a warm-state blob to the config store alongside the authoritative X%. The blob contains: x_percent_authoritative, hysteresis_counter, last_direction, directional_lock_until, an append-only rolling_delta_log of {timestamp, delta_signed_pp} retained for ≥24 hours, a denormalized daily_delta_consumed sum, bound_exhaustion_flags, manual_override_active (plus clamped override value), and last_processed_telemetry_ts.

2. Cold-Boot Reload Sequence — On restart, before opening the telemetry loop: load the warm-state blob; if absent or unreadable, fall back to the initial live calibration X% with a full 3 pp budget and hysteresis counter 0. Restore x_percent_authoritative directly into memory—never recompute from raw telemetry history or replay steps. Rehydrate the rolling 24-hour budget by scanning rolling_delta_log, discarding entries older than (restart_time − 24 h), and recomputing daily_delta_consumed as the sum of absolute surviving deltas. Restore hysteresis, last direction, and reinstate any future directional lock. If bound-exhaustion flags are set, disable auto-stepping in that direction and emit a CRITICAL BOUND_EXHAUST_RESTORE event. If a manual override is active, clamp it to hard bounds, apply immediately, pause auto-stepping, and log OVERRIDE_RESTORED.

3. Hysteresis Warmth Without Replay — The restored hysteresis counter resumes at its saved value but is advanced only by fresh post-restart telemetry readings. The controller must not synthesize readings from the outage gap. On the first fresh cycle: if the reading aligns with last_direction, increment the counter; if it contradicts, reset to 1 in the new direction (or 0 on neutral). This ensures a post-crash spike cannot single-handedly trigger a step.

4. Idempotency and No-Replay Guarantee — rolling_delta_log is used exclusively for budget accounting and is never reapplied to mutate X% on reload. The authoritative X% is taken solely from x_percent_authoritative in the blob. On the first fresh cycle, emit a structured WARM_START telemetry record (restored X%, hysteresis count, remaining budget, lock status, bound flags, override state) to create an auditable checkpoint.

5. Mid-Cycle Crash Safety — If the controller crashes before completing the atomic snapshot, the next boot loads the previous cycle’s committed blob. Because the truncated cycle never wrote a new delta or updated the hysteresis counter, the state is inherently safe: the uncommitted step is lost, which is correct behavior (no replay). The 24-hour budget is unchanged because the delta was never appended.

6. Daily Cap Exhaustion on Restart — If rehydration shows daily_delta_consumed ≥ 3.0 pp, the controller enters DELTA_CAP_EXHAUSTED state. All auto-steps are blocked; telemetry observation and logging continue. Any emergency signal triggers a CONFLICT event and a manual-review alert. The controller exits this state only when aged-out log entries free headroom or a human sets x_percent_manual_override.

7. Downstream Pairlist Consistency — The strategy class remains agnostic to calibration. The Freqtrade pairlist callback (RemotePairList) reads X% from the same config store. To minimize drift during controller restart, the reload routine immediately republishes the restored x_percent_authoritative to the config store with a warm_start timestamp, ensuring the callback picks up the authoritative value on its next refresh cycle rather than operating on a stale gate.

title: Seven-Point Warm-Start and Crash-Recovery Protocol for the External Telemetry Controller
content:
Focus question: What warm-start and crash-recovery protocol should the external telemetry controller use to restore hysteresis counters, rolling 24-hour delta budgets, and last-known X% across restarts without breaching the daily ±3 pp cap or replaying steps?

The external telemetry controller—owner of the step state machine enforcing a daily ±3 pp rolling-window cap, 2-reading hysteresis with a directional reversal lock, and authoritative X% persisted at every rank-refresh cycle—must implement the following seven-point crash-recovery contract.

1. Atomic Snapshot Contract: At the end of every rank-refresh cycle, atomically write a warm-state blob to the config store alongside the authoritative X%. The blob contains: x_percent_authoritative, hysteresis_counter, last_direction, directional_lock_until, an append-only rolling_delta_log of {timestamp, delta_signed_pp} retained for at least 24 hours, a denormalized daily_delta_consumed sum, bound_exhaustion_flags, manual_override_active (plus a clamped override value), and last_processed_telemetry_ts.

2. Cold-Boot Reload Sequence: On restart, before opening the telemetry loop, load the warm-state blob; if absent or unreadable, fall back to the initial live calibration X% with a full 3 pp budget and hysteresis counter set to 0. Restore x_percent_authoritative directly into memory—never recompute from raw telemetry history or replay steps. Rehydrate the rolling 24-hour budget by scanning rolling_delta_log, discarding entries older than (restart_time − 24 h), and recomputing daily_delta_consumed as the sum of absolute surviving deltas. Restore hysteresis, last direction, and reinstate any future directional lock. If bound-exhaustion flags are set, disable auto-stepping in that direction and emit a CRITICAL BOUND_EXHAUST_RESTORE event. If a manual override is active, clamp it to hard bounds, apply immediately, pause auto-stepping, and log OVERRIDE_RESTORED.

3. Hysteresis Warmth Without Replay: The restored hysteresis counter resumes at its saved value but is advanced only by fresh post-restart telemetry readings. The controller must not synthesize readings from the outage gap. On the first fresh cycle: if the reading aligns with last_direction, increment the counter; if it contradicts, reset to 1 in the new direction (or 0 on neutral). This ensures a post-crash spike cannot single-handedly trigger a step.

4. Idempotency and No-Replay Guarantee: rolling_delta_log is used exclusively for budget accounting and is never reapplied to mutate X% on reload. The authoritative X% is taken solely from x_percent_authoritative in the blob. On the first fresh cycle, emit a structured WARM_START telemetry record (restored X%, hysteresis count, remaining budget, lock status, bound flags, override state) to create an auditable checkpoint.

5. Mid-Cycle Crash Safety: If the controller crashes before completing the atomic snapshot, the next boot loads the previous cycle’s committed blob. Because the truncated cycle never wrote a new delta or updated the hysteresis counter, the state is inherently safe: the uncommitted step is lost, which is correct behavior (no replay). The 24-hour budget is unchanged because the delta was never appended.

6. Daily Cap Exhaustion on Restart: If rehydration shows daily_delta_consumed ≥ 3.0 pp, the controller enters DELTA_CAP_EXHAUSTED state. All auto-steps are blocked; telemetry observation and logging continue. Any emergency signal triggers a CONFLICT event and a manual-review alert. The controller exits this state only when aged-out log entries free headroom or a human sets x_percent_manual_override.

7. Downstream Pairlist Consistency: The strategy class remains agnostic to calibration. The Freqtrade pairlist callback (RemotePairList) reads X% from the same config store. To minimize drift during controller restart, the reload routine immediately republishes the restored x_percent_authoritative to the config store with a warm_start timestamp, ensuring the callback picks up the authoritative value on its next refresh cycle rather than operating on a stale gate.

title: Seven-Point Warm-Start and Crash-Recovery Protocol for the External Telemetry Controller
content:
Focus question: What warm-start and crash-recovery protocol should the external telemetry controller use to restore hysteresis counters, rolling 24-hour delta budgets, and last-known X% across restarts without breaching the daily ±3 pp cap or replaying steps?

The external telemetry controller—owner of the step state machine enforcing a daily ±3 pp rolling-window cap, 2-reading hysteresis with a directional reversal lock, and authoritative X% persisted at every rank-refresh cycle—must implement the following seven-point crash-recovery contract.

1. Atomic Snapshot Contract: At the end of every rank-refresh cycle, atomically write a warm-state blob to the config store alongside the authoritative X%. The blob must contain: x_percent_authoritative, hysteresis_counter, last_direction, directional_lock_until, an append-only rolling_delta_log of {timestamp, delta_signed_pp} retained for at least 24 hours, a denormalized daily_delta_consumed sum, bound_exhaustion_flags, manual_override_active (plus a clamped override value), and last_processed_telemetry_ts.

2. Cold-Boot Reload Sequence: On restart, before opening the telemetry loop, load the warm-state blob; if absent or unreadable, fall back to the initial live calibration X% with a full 3 pp budget and hysteresis counter set to 0. Restore x_percent_authoritative directly into memory—never recompute from raw telemetry history or replay steps. Rehydrate the rolling 24-hour budget by scanning rolling_delta_log, discarding entries older than (restart_time − 24 h), and recomputing daily_delta_consumed as the sum of absolute surviving deltas. Restore hysteresis, last direction, and reinstate any future directional lock. If bound-exhaustion flags are set, disable auto-stepping in that direction and emit a CRITICAL BOUND_EXHAUST_RESTORE event. If a manual override is active, clamp it to hard bounds, apply immediately, pause auto-stepping, and log OVERRIDE_RESTORED.

3. Hysteresis Warmth Without Replay: The restored hysteresis counter resumes at its saved value but is advanced only by fresh post-restart telemetry readings. The controller must not synthesize readings from the outage gap. On the first fresh cycle: if the reading aligns with last_direction, increment the counter; if it contradicts, reset to 1 in the new direction (or 0 on neutral). This ensures a post-crash spike cannot single-handedly trigger a step.

4. Idempotency and No-Replay Guarantee: rolling_delta_log is used exclusively for budget accounting and is never reapplied to mutate X% on reload. The authoritative X% is taken solely from x_percent_authoritative in the blob. On the first fresh cycle, emit a structured WARM_START telemetry record (restored X%, hysteresis count, remaining budget, lock status, bound flags, override state) to create an auditable checkpoint.

5. Mid-Cycle Crash Safety: If the controller crashes before completing the atomic snapshot, the next boot loads the previous cycle’s committed blob. Because the truncated cycle never wrote a new delta or updated the hysteresis counter, the state is inherently safe: the uncommitted step is lost, which is correct behavior (no replay). The 24-hour budget is unchanged because the delta was never appended.

6. Daily Cap Exhaustion on Restart: If rehydration shows daily_delta_consumed ≥ 3.0 pp, the controller enters DELTA_CAP_EXHAUSTED state. All auto-steps are blocked; telemetry observation and logging continue. Any emergency signal triggers a CONFLICT event and a manual-review alert. The controller exits this state only when aged-out log entries free headroom or a human sets x_percent_manual_override.

7. Downstream Pairlist Consistency: The strategy class remains agnostic to calibration. The Freqtrade pairlist callback (RemotePairList) reads X% from the same config store. To minimize drift during controller restart, the reload routine immediately republishes the restored x_percent_authoritative to the config store with a warm_start timestamp, ensuring the callback picks up the authoritative value on its next refresh cycle rather than operating on a stale gate.

title: Seven-Point Warm-Start and Crash-Recovery Protocol for the External Telemetry Controller
content:
Focus question: What warm-start and crash-recovery protocol should the external telemetry controller use to restore hysteresis counters, rolling 24-hour delta budgets, and last-known X% across restarts without breaching the daily ±3 pp cap or replaying steps?

The external telemetry controller—owner of the step state machine enforcing a daily ±3 pp rolling-window cap, 2-reading hysteresis with a directional reversal lock, and authoritative X% persisted at every rank-refresh cycle—must implement the following seven-point crash-recovery contract derived from the indexed constraints.

1. Atomic Snapshot Contract: At the end of every rank-refresh cycle, the controller atomically writes a warm-state blob to the config store alongside the authoritative X%. The blob must contain: x_percent_authoritative, hysteresis_counter, last_direction, directional_lock_until, an append-only rolling_delta_log of {timestamp, delta_signed_pp} retained for at least 24 hours, a denormalized daily_delta_consumed sum, bound_exhaustion_flags, manual_override_active (plus a clamped override value), and last_processed_telemetry_ts.

2. Cold-Boot Reload Sequence: On restart, before opening the telemetry loop, load the warm-state blob; if absent or unreadable, fall back to the initial live calibration X% with a full 3 pp budget and hysteresis counter set to 0. Restore x_percent_authoritative directly into memory—never recompute from raw telemetry history or replay steps. Rehydrate the rolling 24-hour budget by scanning rolling_delta_log, discarding entries older than (restart_time − 24 h), and recomputing daily_delta_consumed as the sum of absolute surviving deltas. Restore hysteresis, last direction, and reinstate any future directional lock. If bound-exhaustion flags are set, disable auto-stepping in that direction and emit a CRITICAL BOUND_EXHAUST_RESTORE event. If a manual override is active, clamp it to hard bounds, apply immediately, pause auto-stepping, and log OVERRIDE_RESTORED.

3. Hysteresis Warmth Without Replay: The restored hysteresis counter resumes at its saved value but is advanced only by fresh post-restart telemetry readings. The controller must not synthesize readings from the outage gap. On the first fresh cycle: if the reading aligns with last_direction, increment the counter; if it contradicts, reset to 1 in the new direction (or 0 on neutral). This ensures a post-crash spike cannot single-handedly trigger a step.

4. Idempotency and No-Replay Guarantee: rolling_delta_log is used exclusively for budget accounting and is never reapplied to mutate X% on reload. The authoritative X% is taken solely from x_percent_authoritative in the blob. On the first fresh cycle, emit a structured WARM_START telemetry record (restored X%, hysteresis count, remaining budget, lock status, bound flags, override state) to create an auditable checkpoint.

5. Mid-Cycle Crash Safety: If the controller crashes before completing the atomic snapshot, the next boot loads the previous cycle’s committed blob. Because the truncated cycle never wrote a new delta or updated the hysteresis counter, the state is inherently safe: the uncommitted step is lost, which is correct behavior (no replay). The 24-hour budget is unchanged because the delta was never appended.

6. Daily Cap Exhaustion on Restart: If rehydration shows daily_delta_consumed ≥ 3.0 pp, the controller enters DELTA_CAP_EXHAUSTED state. All auto-steps are blocked; telemetry observation and logging continue. Any emergency signal triggers a CONFLICT event and a manual-review alert. The controller exits this state only when aged-out log entries free headroom or a human sets x_percent_manual_override.

7. Downstream Pairlist Consistency: The strategy class remains agnostic to calibration. The Freqtrade pairlist callback (RemotePairList) reads X% from the same config store. To minimize drift during controller restart, the reload routine immediately republishes the restored x_percent_authoritative to the config store with a warm_start timestamp, ensuring the callback picks up the authoritative value on its next refresh cycle rather than operating on a stale gate.
